plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 27: Direct-Current Circuits
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two drawings of the same circuit side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them. Each is a rectangle split by a single vertical wire into two adjacent loops. Two blue zigzag resistor symbols sit along the top wire, labeled R1 = 3.00 ohms on the left and R3 = 3.00 ohms on the right. The dividing branch carries R2 = 3.00 ohms and the right-hand vertical wire carries R4 = 4.00 ohms, while the left-hand vertical wire is a plain conductor. Two battery symbols sit along the bottom: V1 = 24.00 V in the left loop, plus terminal on the left, and V2 = 29.00 V in the right loop, plus terminal on the right. Panel (b) repeats every element unchanged and adds six teal dots at the corners and branch points, lettered a, b, and c across the top and f, e, and d across the bottom. Setting the bare circuit beside the lettered copy separates the physical layout from the labels laid over it. The pair prepares a multi-loop network for analysis with Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules, the two points where three wires meet serving as the junctions.

interactionPlan.concept: Kirchhoff's rules turn a multi-loop circuit picture into solvable equations: at every junction the currents balance (junction rule), and around every closed loop the signed voltage rises and drops sum to zero (loop rule).
elements: outer rectangular wire frame divided by a central vertical branch into a left loop and a right loop
left vertical wire (plain conductor, no component)
top-left resistor zigzag R1, label 'R1 = 3.00 Ω'
top-right resistor zigzag R3, label 'R3 = 3.00 Ω'
central vertical resistor zigzag R2, label 'R2 = 3.00 Ω'
right vertical resistor zigzag R4, label 'R4 = 4.00 Ω'
bottom-left battery symbol V1 with '+' terminal on left and '−' on right, label 'V1 = 24.00 V'
bottom-right battery symbol V2 with '−' terminal on left and '+' on right, label 'V2 = 29.00 V'
six teal node dots with letter labels a (top-left), b (top-center), c (top-right), f (bottom-left), e (bottom-center), d (bottom-right) — visible only in labeled view
branch current direction arrows (revealed when a junction is clicked)
Kirchhoff current equation callout near the clicked junction (e.g. I1 = I2 + I3 at b)
loop-traversal highlight overlay on the selected closed path
accumulated signed-voltage sum callout (ΣV = 0) that grows as the loop is traced

interactions.label: Circuit view
interactions.teaches: The lettered nodes and dots are analysis scaffolding laid over the exact same physical circuit — no battery or resistor changes, only the labels needed to write equations appear.

Clicking a junction (b or e, the two points where three wires meet) highlights the three connected branches and shows that the currents entering must equal the currents leaving — Kirchhoff's junction rule, a statement of charge conservation.

interactions.label: Loop to trace
interactions.teaches: The loop rule can be applied to any closed path; choosing the left or right loop selects which set of components the voltage sum is written over.

interactions.label: Trace loop
interactions.teaches: Stepping around the chosen loop highlights each resistor and battery in traversal order and accumulates a signed voltage term (a rise across a battery's + terminal, a drop across a resistor in the current's direction), making clear that the total around the closed path returns to zero.

demo_steps.title: The physical circuit
demo_steps.narration: Two adjacent loops share a central branch: R1 and V1 on the left, R3 and R4 on the right, with R2 in the middle. This is the circuit exactly as built, with no analysis labels.

demo_steps.title: Add the scaffolding
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the labeled view drops teal dots and letters a–f onto the same circuit. The two three-way meeting points, b and e, are the junctions where the current rule will apply.

demo_steps.title: Junction rule at b
demo_steps.narration: Click junction b (or e): the three branches meeting there light up with current arrows and a balance equation appears — whatever current flows in must flow out, so the branch currents are linked.

demo_steps.title: Loop rule, left loop
demo_steps.narration: Select the left loop and step through the trace: R1, R2, and V1 highlight in order while signed voltage terms accumulate, ending at ΣV = 0 around the closed path.

demo_steps.title: Loop rule, right loop
demo_steps.narration: Now trace the right loop: R3, R4, V2, and the shared R2 highlight in order with their own signed terms, again closing to zero — the shared R2 appears in both loop equations, coupling them.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A multi-loop circuit is solved by writing one current-balance equation per junction and one signed-voltage-sum-equals-zero equation per independent loop; the node letters and the chosen traversal direction are the scaffolding that convert the drawing into those equations.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render one panel at a time per the view toggle (do not show (a) and (b) side by side). Lay out a wide rectangle split by a central vertical wire into two equal loops. Draw resistors as blue zigzag symbols: R1 top-left, R3 top-right, R2 on the central branch, R4 on the right edge; the left edge is a plain wire. Draw batteries on the bottom wire as long/short parallel-line symbols with explicit '+' and '−' marks (V1 plus on left, V2 plus on right) and value labels above. In labeled view add small teal filled dots at the six corners/branch points with italic letters a,b,c across the top and f,e,d across the bottom. On junction click, tint the three incident branches and draw red current arrows plus a small equation callout (e.g. 'I1 = I2 + I3'). On loop trace, highlight the traversed components in a warm color (orange) one at a time and show a running 'ΣV = ...' callout that resolves to 0 at 'done'. Keep all component values and polarity identical between the two views so the only change is the appearance of the labels.

authoredContext:
Consider the circuit in the figure(a). Let us analyze this circuit to find the current through each resistor. First, label the circuit as shown in part (b).

(a) A multi-loop circuit. (b) Label the circuit to help with orientation.

Part a shows a circuit with two horizontal branches and three vertical branches. The first horizontal branch has two resistors of 3 Ω each and the second branch has two voltage sources of 24 V with positive terminal on the left and 29 V with positive terminal on the right. The left vertical branch is directly connected, the middle branch has a resistance of 3 Ω and the right branch has a resistance of 4 Ω. Part b shows the same circuit as part a with labelled junctions

Next, determine the junctions. In this circuit, points b and e each have three wires connected, making them junctions. Start to apply Kirchhoff’s junction rule (∑ Iin=∑ Iout) by drawing arrows representing the currents and labeling each arrow, as shown in the figure(b). Junction b shows that I1=I2+I3 and Junction e shows that I2+I3=I1. Since Junction e gives the same information of Junction b, it can be disregarded. This circuit has three unknowns, so we need three linearly independent equations to analyze it.

discrepancies: The source is a two-panel side-by-side layout (a) and (b); the generated figure uses a single-panel toggle between views, which is acceptable but changes the at-a-glance comparison the source provides

The source panel (b) shows node dots as filled green/teal circles at all six nodes simultaneously alongside the circuit; the generated figure hides them behind a toggle, so the default screenshot only shows panel (a)

The battery symbols in the generated figure use 4 alternating long/short vertical lines which is correct, but the visual weight and spacing appear slightly more compressed than the source's battery symbols
evaluation.notes: Excellent implementation of a Kirchhoff's laws circuit figure: topology, component values, battery polarities, and node labels all match the source exactly; the interactive junction-rule and loop-rule tracing with step-by-step voltage-term accumulation is pedagogically rich and conceptually correct, with the only structural deviation being the two-panel source converted to a toggle-based single panel.
action_items: Consider showing both views simultaneously (side-by-side) or at least making the default state show panel (b) with node labels, since the labeled view is the more information-rich panel and the source presents both at once
Slightly increase label font size (from 15 to 17-18) to improve readability at inline rendering sizes

feedback.rationale: All scores are 4-5 with no failure modes, the concept is accurately implemented with rich interactivity, and the remaining action items are minor polish suggestions that don't warrant another iteration.
